concept: One lime signal on black: the enquiry is the only lit thing in the picture, from the form to the CRM.
One minute told as three moments: the tap, the clock, the buzz in a pocket. Cobalt and butter yellow.
Highlight cover for Web + CRM: two rings linked, website and CRM joined. Sits inside the circle crop.

Contrast as the picture, in plum and blush. The cover asks the question in words too faint to read, tagged 1.5:1; the statistic is set as an eye-test chart that fades row by row; the last frame answers in the same words at full strength, tagged 15.5:1.

A web address set the way it sounds down the phone: six lines of spoken words with every hyphen lit in lilac, one giant 4 nobody can hear, then the fix said once on a single line. Deep green, lilac and cream.

A type specimen that misbehaves, in red, cream and ink. The hook sets fourteen letters in fourteen typefaces at one cap height; four places a business shows its name each wear their own face; one ampersand shuffles through seven faces and stops on one; the same four words roll over into that one face.

A year built as one lit ring, seen three ways. Lying in space at 99% uptime, with a 1% gap to find. Then right up against that gap, the ring now two glowing blocks with 3.65 days set through the break. Then from inside at 99.9%, a horizon with a hairline cut. Graphite and ice blue.
One photograph, one question. A yellow rotary phone on a yellow field, set inside the same margins as the question it can't answer: who rang at 2pm. Yolk yellow and ink, nothing else.

A keyboard with one key missing, zooming in: five keys across the frame spell http and the fifth is an empty recess with a ghost of the s; then two, the p and the hole; then one, the s back in place in blue. Silver deck, white keys, one blue key.

One business card for a made-up joiner, seen three ways. Lying in space, with a dry line about its last line. Then right up against that line, out of focus above it, with @gmail.com run over in highlighter. Then standing and facing us with the email moved to the firm's own address, so the two lines match letter for letter under one stroke of the same highlighter. Petrol teal, cotton white and aqua.

The front panel of an old beige office computer, and one button in three beats. Light off under the oldest question in IT; right up against it, pressed, light on green; then larger and running off the frame, light off again. Putty plastic, dark ink and one green light.

One five-second stopwatch with a sky-blue dial, shot close up and off centre four ways. At the head of the dial the hand stands on zero beside the question, then goes. At the foot it stops on 2.5, where the flange stops being navy. At the shoulder it stops on 4, where the flange turns red. Then the camera pulls back to the hub as the hand flies back to zero beside 'Time yours.' and the address. Sky-blue enamel, navy print, steel, and one red hand.
